title: Dental SEO: How to Get More Patients from Search
excerpt: A step-by-step guide to dental SEO: Google Business Profile, reviews, treatment pages, local search, content, cost and common mistakes.

meta.rl_answer: Dental SEO is the work of making a dental practice easy to find in Google, Maps and AI search. Start with a complete Google Business Profile and a steady flow of honest reviews, then build one clear page for each treatment, answer patient questions, fix technical basics and track calls and bookings.
meta.rl_takeaways:
Dental SEO is mostly local. Your Google Business Profile and reviews often matter as much as your website.
Give each main treatment its own page with who it suits, how it works, who does it and how to book.
Ask all patients for reviews, reply to every one and never share a patient's private details.
Keep your name, address and phone the same everywhere.
Have a dentist check health content, and do not promise results.
Track calls, bookings and Search Console data, not only rankings.
Google says changes can take hours to months, so judge results after about six months.
meta.rl_faqs:
What is dental SEO? | Dental SEO is the set of steps that help a dental practice appear in Google, Google Maps and AI search when patients look for a dentist or a treatment. It covers your website, your Google Business Profile, reviews and helpful content.
Why is SEO important for dentists? | Patients search before they call. If your practice does not appear, a competitor gets the booking. SEO also builds steady traffic that keeps working after you stop paying for ads.
How do I rank higher for dentist near me searches? | Complete and keep your Google Business Profile accurate, collect honest reviews, keep your name, address and phone the same everywhere, and build clear location and treatment pages on a fast site that works on phones.
How long does dental SEO take? | Google says some changes show in hours and others take months. Fixing a profile and collecting reviews can help within weeks. Pages that rank for treatment searches usually take several months.
How much does dental SEO cost? | There is no standard price. It depends on your number of locations, how competitive your area is, how much content you need and who does the work. Get written quotes and compare the scope, not only the price.
Do Google reviews help dental SEO? | Yes. Reviews are a factor in local results and they strongly affect whether a patient books. Ask all patients, reply to every review and never share private patient details in a reply.
What pages does a dental website need? | A home page, one page for each main treatment, a team page, a contact and booking page, a page for each location, and a prices or how we price page if you can share it.
Can I do dental SEO myself? | Yes, for one location. Start with your Google Business Profile, reviews and treatment pages. A specialist can help with several locations, large content plans and reporting.
What should I ask a dental SEO agency? | Ask for a written scope and price, who writes the content, how reports link to calls and bookings, how they earn links, their experience with health practices and how you can leave the contract. Be wary of promises of a ranking date.
Does dental SEO work for AI search? | The same steps help. Give clear, direct answers, keep your facts consistent across your site and listings, show named dentists with qualifications and earn real reviews. No method guarantees an AI tool will name your practice.

meta.rl_g_glossary:
NAP | Name, address and phone number. They should match everywhere online.
Google Business Profile | Your free listing in Google Search and Maps, with hours, photos, reviews and a booking link.
Local SEO | Work that helps a business appear in searches tied to a place.
Schema markup | Code that tells search engines what a page is about, such as a business, its address and its reviews.
Search intent | The reason behind a search: to learn, to compare or to book.
